title: Bexarotene in WWOX-LoF
summary: A test of sterol delivery during first myelination.

graph.evidence: Apoe increased while Abcg1 decreased in two treated mouse cell classes.
graph.inference: A higher lipid-carrier signal leaves sterol transfer unresolved.
graph.hypothesis: Lipid supply and recipient metabolism can limit distinct steps in WWOX.
graph.experiment: Trace sterol to new sheaths under donor and recipient controls.

evidence: Apoe rose and Abcg1 fell in microglia and mature oligodendrocyte gates in four treated versus four control APP/PS1 mice. Both directions survive two gate thresholds and every single-animal omission.
inference: LXR transcripts fell in three held WWOX models. Exporter RNA changes differed by tissue. Neither RNA observation measures sterol transfer.
hypothesis: Bexarotene could change sterol synthesis or retention in oligodendrocytes even if donor export stays limited.
experiment: At matched exposure, interrupt donor export or recipient RXR and include a lipidated-carrier bypass. Measure label in first compact sheaths and conduction at matched recruitment.
limits: Retain as a laboratory probe. The adult MS primary efficacy endpoint missed its target. All 26 bexarotene recipients developed hypothyroidism. Pediatric CNS exposure remains unresolved.
